text: Sir Adrian Frederick Melhuish Smith, FRS (born 9 September 1946), is a British statistician who served as chief executive of the Alan Turing Institute from 2018 to 2023 and as president of the Royal Society from 2020 to 2025. He was born in Dawlish, Devon, and received his education at Selwyn College, Cambridge, and University College London, where his PhD supervisor was Dennis Lindley. From 1977 to 1990, he was professor of statistics and head of the mathematics department at the University of Nottingham, followed by a position at Imperial College, London, where he also served as head of the mathematics department. Smith was a former deputy vice-chancellor of the University of London and became vice-chancellor on 1 September 2012, stepping down in August 2018 to become director of the Alan Turing Institute. He is a member of the governing body of the London Business School and served on the Advisory Council for the Office for National Statistics from 1996 to 1998, as statistical advisor to the Nuclear Waste Inspectorate from 1991 to 1998, and as advisor on Operational Analysis to the Ministry of Defence from 1982 to 1987. He was a former president of the Royal Statistical Society, elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2001, with his FRS citation highlighting "his diverse contributions to Bayesian statistics. His monographs are the most comprehensive available and his work has had a major impact on the development of monitoring tools for clinicians." In statistical theory, Smith is a proponent of Bayesian statistics and evidence-based practice, extending evidence-based medicine into public policy. With Antonio Machi, he translated Bruno de Finetti's Theory of Probability into English. He co-authored an influential 1990 paper with Alan E. Gelfand on the Gibbs sampler technique for Bayesian numerical integration and was co-author of the seminal paper on the particle filter (Gordon, Salmond and Smith, 1993). In mathematics and statistics education, he led the team that produced the Smith Report on secondary mathematics education in the United Kingdom. In April 2008, he was appointed director general of science and research at the Department for Innovation, Universities and Skills, taking up the role in September 2008 with an annual remuneration of £160,000. He was knighted in the 2011 New Year Honours and appeared as a guest on The Life Scientific on BBC Radio 4 in 2023. In 2011, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Science from Plymouth University in 2015, an Honorary Doctorate of Science from Ohio State University, and in 2020, an Honorary Doctorate Honoris Causa from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro. He also received Honorary Doctorates from City University, University of Loughborough, Queen Mary, and University of London.
